title: Score the guess
description: Have the riddle keeper's scoring hand its answer back, so the rest of the game can use it.

tasks.title: Hand an answer back
tasks.body: return sends a value back to the line that called the function. With def double(n): return n * 2, the line x = double(4) stores 8. print() inside a function only shows text: the caller gets nothing it can use.
tasks.detail: return also ends the function at once, so lines after it in the same block never run. A function with no return gives back None. return a, b gives back two values together, and low, high = pair() unpacks them into two names.

tasks.code:
# Points for a riddle, worked out in one place
def points(tries):
    if tries == 1:
        return 10
    return 10 - tries * 2

total = points(1) + points(3)
print(total)
print(points(2))
tasks.note: points() hands back a number, so two calls can be added together. When tries is 1 the first return ends the function, so the second return never runs.

tasks.question: Suppose both return lines in points() were print() lines instead. What would total = points(1) + points(3) do?
tasks.why: A function that only prints gives back None, and None + None is a TypeError. print() shows a number; return hands it back to be used.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: add print(points(5)) and work out the answer before you run it. Then change points() so that 5 or more tries scores 0, with one more if and return.

Write score(secret, guess), which returns 10 if the guess is right, 5 if it is no more than 2 away, 1 if it is no more than 10 away, and 0 otherwise. Then write verdict(secret, guess), which returns two values: the score, and True if the guess is too high or False if it is not. Return the answers; do not print them. Your program should not ask for input: the check calls your functions with its own values.
tasks.starter: # Define score(secret, guess) and verdict(secret, guess)
hints: Work out how far apart the two numbers are first, ignoring which is bigger: abs() gives a number without its minus sign, so abs(3 - 7) is 4. Then check the closest band first, and return as soon as one matches.
verdict() can call score() instead of repeating its rules, then return the score and a comparison together, separated by a comma.
The same shape with other names: def grade(mark): with if mark >= 90: return "A" first, then the lower bands, and a last return for everything else.

error_hints.text: Use the parameters from the def line inside the function, spelled the same way.
Check that each function takes two values, the secret and then the guess, and that score() returns a number in every case.
score(50, 50) should return 10. If the check says your function returned None, it printed the answer instead of returning it.
48 is exactly 2 away from 50, and no more than 2 away includes 2 itself.
verdict(20, 25) should return 1 and True together: return the score, a comma, and whether the guess is bigger.
Check a guess more than 10 away: every guess needs a score, so the function needs a return for the last band too.
Check a guess just below the secret: too high means bigger than the secret, not just different from it.

similar_example.note: Bands checked from the top, each ending the function with return. Your score() measures distance instead of marks.

other_ways.note: elif and else make it clear that exactly one band applies. verdict() reuses score().
The bands as a list of pairs: the loop returns from the first band the gap fits. Adding a band means adding a pair.
